tenderEligibilityCriterionList.description: Bidders shall not be under a declaration of ineligibility for corrupt and fraudulent practices issued by Government of Karnataka

It shall be the responsibility of the Bidder to ensure credit of Tender Processing Fee and EMD into the respective receiving bank accounts of e-Procurement on or before the last date and time of bid submission.
EMD Payments through e-Payment mode shall be made as one single transaction and payments made in part are liable for rejection.
All the terms & Conditions as per the Tender Document

tenderTechnicalCriterionList.description: Experience in feasibility study, DFR, DPR, financial modelling or PPP structuring for healthcare-sector PPP projects. (a)5 marks for each Eligible Assignment satisfying Clause 2.2.2(A), subject to a maximum of 20 marks.(b)The assignment shall involve feasibility assessment, DFR/DPR, financial modelling or PPP structuring for a healthcare-sector PPP project with an underlying project cost of at least INR 10 crore.(c)Supporting evidence may comprise any one or a combination of the documents permitted under Clause 2.2.2(A).

Experience in bid-process management for healthcare-sector PPP projects, including preparation of RFP/concession documents and bid evaluation. At least one assignment submitted across Criteria 1.1 and 1.2 shall relate to cardiac care or a Cath Lab, and at least one assignment under Criterion 1.2 shall be a successfully closed healthcare-sector PPP transaction. The two requirements may be satisfied through the same or separate assignments.(a)5 marks for each Eligible Assignment satisfying Clause 2.2.2(A), subject to a maximum of 20 marks.(b)The assignment shall involve healthcare PPP bid-process management, including preparation of tender/concession documents and bid evaluation, for an underlying project cost of at least INR 10 crore. (c)An integrated transaction advisory assignment may be counted under both Criteria 1.1 and 1.2 where the supporting evidence establishes performance of both scopes. The mandatory transaction-closure requirement shall apply independently. (d)Supporting evidence may comprise any one or a combination of the documents permitted under Clause 2.2.2(A).

Approach & Methodology (a) Presentation on the proposed operationalisation strategy, existing-asset and operational-readiness assessment, cardiac-care service-delivery model, PPP structure, risk allocation, procurement approach and assignment methodology.(b) Presentation of relevant innovations, technology considerations and case studies relating to operation and management of cardiac-care facilities and healthcare PPP transactions.
Work plan (a) Presentation on Work Plan (Implementation Schedule).(b)Experience of other personnel involved apart from proposed Key Personnel. Deployment of Project Team. etc.
